articles.title: ‘A child pretending to be an adult’: Vanity Fair publishes scathing Taylor Swift exposé from over 100 sources
articles.summary: Taylor Swift is the biggest pop star on the planet, and she has spent much of her career being celebrated as a generous friend, a champion for artists’ right...
articles.body:
Taylor Swift is the biggest pop star on the planet, and she has spent much of her career being celebrated as a generous friend, a champion for artists' rights, and an underdog who fought her way to the top. But a new magazine profile is telling a very different story.

The lengthy profile, published on Monday, is built on interviews with more than 100 sources. It describes Swift as controlling and "punitive," and it questions nearly every part of the image she has built for herself.

Few artists have shaped their own public narrative as carefully as Swift. For years, she has described herself as an outsider growing up, saying in interviews that her friends abandoned her as a kid. Her songs have turned her breakups, feuds, and business battles into chapters of a story with her as the protagonist, and often as the one who was wronged.

The biggest of those battles came in 2019, when music executive Scooter Braun acquired her former label, Big Machine, and with it the masters to her first six albums. Swift responded with a scathing post on Tumblr , accusing Braun of "incessant, manipulative bullying," and she went on to re-record those albums as "Taylor's Version." Her fans rallied behind her, and in 2025, she bought back the original recordings , which was widely celebrated as a win for artists' rights.

Swift has also been involved in plenty of public feuds over the years, including with Kim Kardashian and Kanye West, Katy Perry, and more recently Charli XCX. Charli's 2024 song "Sympathy is a knife" was widely believed to be about Swift, and Swift's "Actually Romantic" from The Life of a Showgirl was seen as a pointed response . Earlier this month, Swift appeared to put an end to feud rumors with former friend Karlie Kloss at a Kansas City Chiefs game.

Through it all, her popularity has only grown. Her Eras Tour became the highest-grossing tour of all time, she became a billionaire in 2023, and she married Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce in a high-profile wedding at Madison Square Garden this summer.

But the last few weeks have been rocky. Swift was reportedly urged to "take back control" after details from the wedding leaked, and she has found herself caught in a legal battle over The Life of a Showgirl . Even one self-described superfan recently declared that "the blind love era is over."

Now, Swift faces a rather scathing hit piece.

Vanity Fair's piece , written by May Jeong, never actually uses Swift's name, referring to her only as "The Star," and it gives nicknames to most of the other people involved as well. It is structured like a record, with "A side" sections telling the familiar version of Swift's story and "B side" sections offering a much less flattering one.

Many of the harshest claims come from anonymous sources. A music industry executive, referred to as "The Exec," described Swift bluntly.

The same executive compared Swift's social circle to the villain of Mean Girls , saying, "It's truly Regina George."

Another source, described as a person who used to be close with Swift, said that she "loves to smack people in the head" in a figurative sense, as a way of disciplining people. That source also said Swift has a pattern of cutting people out of her life.

"Nobody is beyond reproach with her. If you don't see it her way, she comes after you," the source said.

The piece also runs through many of Swift's feuds over the years, including her rift with Katy Perry, who is referred to as "The California Girl." Jeong described Perry as "an adult pretending to be a child," and then turned the line around on Swift, writing that she "might be a child pretending to be an adult."

According to Jeong, many people refused to speak on the record, and one former collaborator even advised Jeong to turn down the assignment. Swift declined to comment for the story.

articles.title: Country singer Drake White admits he still fears another stroke seven years after nearly dying
articles.summary: Drake White reveals the fear of another stroke lingers seven years after his hemorrhagic stroke, and how faith and Navy SEALs help him cope.
articles.body: Seven years after suffering a hemorrhagic stroke that nearly killed him in 2019, country music star Drake White admits he still lives with the lingering fear of suffering another medical emergency. Speaking exclusively to Fox News Digital at the third-annual Benefit For The Brain event in Nashville, the 43-year-old singer opened up about the lasting physical and mental toll of his health battle — and how he has learned to channel that anxiety into purpose. "The fear of having another stroke is always there," White said. "Once your nervous system goes through that, it’s imprinted on it. You can work yourself into a tizzy, you can work yourself into anxiety attacks, and your heart rate gets up, your blood pressure gets going. So, it's about learning how to deal with that and breathe through it." COUNTRY SINGER DRAKE WHITE DESCRIBES ‘GUNSHOT’ MOMENT HIS BRAIN RUPTURED MID-CONCERT: ‘I KNEW I WAS DYING’ White credited both his background as an athlete and the support of friends — including several Navy SEALs in attendance at the benefit — with teaching him how to manage anxiety and high-stress situations. "Just being confident in people saying, 'Hey, you're helping, keep going,'" he explained. "Because there are so many days that I don't want to keep going. So yeah, I fear sometimes, but there's a lot of good things in fear, too. You pay attention when you're scared." "For me, I had a real-life experience where I witnessed a near-death experience. To come through that — that'll never leave me. I'm 43 now; I was 35 when that happened. So for me, it's very, very palpable. Very, very real." "The thing is, God meets you where you're at," he added. "I don't care who you are, what you believe or what you think, if you cry out to Jesus, you cry out to God ... God's gonna meet you where you're at, and He's gonna come to you. And that's what happened. It was as clear as that." In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital earlier this year, White reflected further on that life-changing moment and how leaning on his faith carried him through recovery. CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND Before hitting the road with Zac Brown in 2019, White was diagnosed with a rare brain condition called arteriovenous malformation (AVM). Having already undergone four surgeries, White said doctors told him the chance of a rupture was less than 1%. He decided to take the risk and continue touring. His worst nightmare unfolded while doing what he loved most: performing. REALITY STAR DR PIMPLE POPPER SUFFERED A STROKE WHILE FILMING HER SHOW, SAYS PART OF HER BRAIN 'DIED' "We just took the stage in Roanoke, Virginia. It was probably 98 degrees and cotton candy skies, beautiful, 2,500 people out there. And I tore into three or four songs and I just felt a tick," White recalled. "I felt my left arm, my fingers tingling, kind of numbness. And then I heard what I call a gunshot. It literally sounded like an audible gunshot behind my left ear. And when it snapped, if you look at the video back, you can see me trying to push through it." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "I grew up in Alabama where you just kind of keep pushing, keep going, and I tried to do that, and I couldn't speak," he continued. "I couldn't think, and the cotton candy sky became the grass, and the grass became the sky. Everything flipped upside down ... Everything slowed way down, and it just felt like I was walking in quicksand, and everything was heavy. My left arm was heavy, my left foot was heavy, and I knew right then, I was like, 'Well, dang, I'm having a stroke.'" White immediately remembered his doctors' warnings about what would happen if the AVM ruptured. "They told me, 'If it ruptures, you would have a very good chance of death,'" he said. "Death was kind of it. And so I just remember thinking: Keep breathing, keep praying, and get me to the hospital." RUDY GIULIANI REVEALS HE HAD 'SPIRITUAL EXPERIENCE' WHILE IN PNEUMONIA-RELATED COMA White was rushed to a local hospital and administered a coagulant that stopped the brain bleed. "That ultimately saved my life, but in that process, [I] saw angels, had the whole near-death experience, talked to God, the whole thing," he said. "It humbled me down to my knees. I realized that rock bottom had a basement. It really got me to a spot where I didn't know if I was gonna survive." At the time, the country singer was left paralyzed on his left side and uncertain of his future. "That was when the mental battle started," White said. "The doctors came in and told me that I'd had a hemorrhagic stroke and that I had a long road ahead of me. They didn't say this directly, but I heard them murmuring that I'd be lucky to walk again, much less get back on stage." "I was thinking, 'I've put so much time into this, and I've been so passionate about it. What am I going to do now? I've got a bedpan and I can't even feed myself.'" Amid his recovery, White and his wife, Alex, were hit with another tragedy six years after his stroke. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER In September 2025, the couple — who are parents to a 3-year-old son — announced the death of their newborn daughter, Della Elizabeth. During this time, White leaned heavily on his family, friends and faith. Looking back, he describes his previous interaction with God during his near-death experience as "very peaceful." "My faith, I like to describe it like this: The sun feels different on my cheek than it does on your cheek," he said. "I am a Jesus-following guy that believes in that wholeheartedly. Met Him, saw Him, talked to Him. It's as real as me and you talking right now ... He was like, 'What's going on? Tell me what's up. ' It was the most peaceful I'd ever been in my life in that moment." "I was not scared," he continued. "It's just like a transition. I could feel it. It was palpable. You know what I mean? I could touch it ... Whatever faith is for you, it meets you where you are. It meets you where you are in a hospital bed or in a car wreck or whatever it is. It met me where I was." Now, White is turning his new perspective into action through his Benefit For The Brain concert. Following two consecutive sold-out shows, the event’s third installment once again united major musical talent and passionate advocates to raise awareness and funds for brain and mental health. For White, hosting the event is the fulfillment of a vow he made while fighting for his life. "For me, it was just a promise to myself and a promise to God that if He let me out of the hospital — if He would get me to a place where I could live again — that I would help give back to people and show people how I got from the darkness to the light," White said. "If you have a purpose, and you find that purpose and push towards it, then your life starts to make sense. None of that stuff made sense to me when I was going through it — there were a lot of whines and a lot of howls. But when you start seeing other people come up and say, 'Hey, you helped me through this,' or 'You helped me through cancer,' or 'You helped me through losing my son or daughter' — who am I to even be complaining about what I had to go through if I get an opportunity to help people? articles.title: Billy Bob Thornton urges viewers to learn the real history behind Thanksgiving on Fox Nation's 'The Mayflower'
articles.summary: Stars gathered in New York City for the debut screening of Fox Nation's "Billy Bob Thornton Presents: The Mayflower," just in time for Thanksgiving.
articles.body: The stars were out on Monday night in New York City to celebrate Fox Nation’s "Billy Bob Thornton Presents: The Mayflower" as the iconic actor seeks to educate viewers, just in time for Thanksgiving. "The Mayflower," which is now streaming on Fox Nation, is a three-part historical docudrama that aims to strip away the myth of Plymouth Rock and inform viewers on everything from the deadly voyage across the Atlantic to Thanksgiving and one of America’s bloodiest wars. Fox News Media executives, Fox News Channel anchors, the show’s creators and other special guests gathered at The Whitby Hotel for an exclusive screening of the debut episode. "Thank God for Fox Nation, because they’re willing to tell stories of our history, which is awesome," Thornton told the crowd. BILLY BOB THORNTON SAYS HE’S A HOLIDAY ‘PURIST’ AS HE BRINGS BACK ‘TRADITIONAL’ THANKSGIVING AT HOME "The Mayflower" traces the Pilgrims’ death-defying Atlantic crossing, the fragile alliance forged between the English settlers and the Wampanoag people, and the devastating conflict that ultimately transformed Britain’s colonies into the earliest foundations of an American identity. "One of the things that I think we're quickly losing around here is our history. History is very important, and if you don't know where you came from, it's hard to live now," Thornton said. "I love history, I’ve always studied it. My dad was a history teacher, and I always want to learn more about stuff and I didn’t know this," he continued. "I knew the story they told us in elementary school." BILLY BOB THORNTON PUSHES BACK ON CELEBRITY ACTIVISM: ‘I DON'T KNOW ANYTHING ABOUT POLITICS’ The Academy Award-winning writer, actor and director said most people simply think, "’Oh, that’s great, the native tribe came over, and they had turkey'" — but the truth is far more complex. "The people who came over here on [the Mayflower]… a lot of people got sick, a lot of people died," Thornton said. He called for viewers to keep the trials and tribulations of the Pilgrims in mind when celebrating Thanksgiving with loved ones this week. "When you say your blessings to the people, maybe remember the people that suffered to get us where we are," he said. Fox News Media CEO Suzanne Scott, Fox News Media President and Executive Editor Jay Wallace, Fox News Media Chief Digital and Marketing Officer Jason Klarman, Fox News' Bill Hemmer, Dana Perino, Lawrence Jones, Martha MacCallum, Emily Compagno, Eric Shawn, Lisa Boothe, Paul Mauro and "House of Cards" actor Michael Kelly were among the guests for Monday’s screening and cocktail reception. FOX NATION TEAMS UP WITH JACK CARR TO TAKE VIEWERS INSIDE THE GLOBAL MANHUNT FOR CARLOS THE JACKAL While developing "The Mayflower," the team consulted a range of historical resources and experts, including historians at Plimoth Patuxet Museums, where portions of the series were filmed, as well as acclaimed historian Nathaniel Philbrick. The series is produced by AIRtime Projects and Terminal B TV with Thornton as an executive producer, alongside Geyer Kosinski, Tom Forman, David Metzler, Jordan Rosenblum and showrunner and executive producer John Ealer. "My only wish and prayer from you all is that you watch this as people who want to learn something and watch something wonderful that these wonderful producers and director put together with Fox Nation," Thornton said. Thornton currently stars in the hit Paramount+ series, "Landman," for which he received Critics' Choice Award and Golden Globe Award nominations for Best Actor in a Television Drama. His recent projects have also included the Amazon series "Goliath" and the critically acclaimed FX series "Fargo." Thornton has also starred in such movies as "Bad Santa," "The Alamo," "Bandits," "The Man Who Wasn’t There," "Friday Night Lights," "Sling Blade," "A Simple Plan," "Armageddon" and "Monster’s Ball," among other critical and commercial hits.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP CLICK HERE TO SUBSCRIBE TO FOX NATION Fox Nation programs are viewable on demand and from your mobile device app but only for FOX Nation subscribers. articles.title: ‘Naughty’ vs ‘Nasty’: Universal and Warner Bros. Battle Over Titles for New Jennifer Aniston, Jenna Ortega Movies (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros. Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling...
articles.body:
Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros. Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling projects that sound alike and are set to hit theaters around the same time, five sources tell Variety .

The first is "Naughty," Olivia Wilde's raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer Aniston. The other is "Nasty," Mary Bronstein's psychological drama led by Jenna Ortega, which will roll out under Warner's new indie label Clockwork. Universal slated "Naughty" for Nov. 5, 2027, after registering the name with the Motion Picture Association in 2023, according to two sources. Clockwork, the nascent shingle run by Neon veteran Christian Parkes, has not officially set a date for "Nasty," though four sources say the film is also eyeing a November 2027 release.

Generally, studios go to great lengths to avoid delivering movies with similar-sounding names — much less launching them in the same corridor. "Naughty" and "Nasty" aren't alike in genre or subject matter. "Naughty," featuring Aniston and Peter Dinklage, follows a single mom who has to convince Santa Claus to testify at her divorce hearing. "Nasty," Bronstein's follow-up to "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You," revolves around an elite gymnast competing for a spot on the Olympic team while dealing with her manipulative coach.

Yet insiders at Universal and Warner Bros. feel the fact that the titles are basically synonyms could confuse moviegoers. Further complicating the matter is that LuckyChap, Margot Robbie's prolific film and TV production shop, is backing both projects. Universal and Clockwork declined to comment.

The spat is headed toward a formal review by the MPA, which has a 101-year-old department called the Title Registration Bureau to manage such conflicts. Arbitration involves a panel of studio intellectual property lawyers at the ready to hash it out. Although titles are not copyrightable, the TRB is armed with a 50-page document outlining rules of play and precedent, per one source, and its rulings are legally binding. The MPA declined to comment on the matter.

"Movies want to distinguish themselves, and the first way they do that is the title," says Jeff Bock, an analyst with Exhibitor Relations. "If they sound similar, there could be confusion."

Universal believes it should have dibs since it was first to file with "Naughty." That would mean "Nasty" either changes its name or shifts its release date. Insiders note Clockwork filed two alternative titles for "Nasty" with its MPA documentation, but the filmmakers are against using the backups.

Meanwhile, sources close to "Nasty" feel that Universal is "punching down" at Clockwork because the indie drama doesn't have the same broad commercial appeal as the Aniston-led holiday comedy. (Though Clockwork is a specialty label, it is owned and operated by the vast Skydance Motion Picture Group). Wilde is content to let "Nasty" proceed as titled, according to a person familiar with her thinking. LuckyChap is working toward a solution that sets up both projects for success without entering MPA arbitration, two sources add.

Disputes like these rarely become public knowledge, insiders say. And most often, studios work it out without involving the Title Registration Bureau. The group's last two arbitrations were in 2018. That's when Disney and Lucasfilm settled on "Solo: A Star Wars Story" rather than "Solo" to distinguish the Han Solo origin story from the 2018 climbing documentary "Free Solo." And Universal agreed to change its raunchy comedy to "Blockers" from "The Pact," a name that was already used by a 2012 horror film.

Renaming movies can benefit both parties. Ask Paramount and Sony, which released "No Strings Attached" and "Friends With Benefits" a few months apart in 2011. Both romantic comedies — one starring Natalie Portman and Ashton Kutcher and the other with Mila Kunis and Justin Timberlake — had an identical premise involving two friends who agree to casual sex without dating. "No Strings Attached" was originally called "Friends With Benefits," but the studio acquiesced to the title change. Any plot similarities didn't dilute the films' respective box office, with each one grossing $149 million globally.

To that end, movies with similar themes or ideas are less of a problem for studios. Bock points to 1998's "Armageddon" and "Deep Impact," two disaster films about comets on a collision course with Earth. Both were theatrical winners, with "Armageddon" earning $553 million globally and "Deep Impact" generating $350 million globally.

"Consumers might be fooled by something like that, but it didn't affect the box office," he says. "They turned out to be different, even though the synopsis was the same."

Pursuant to judicially authorized warrants, FBI special agents searched the two storage units registered to Markle. Markle has rented both storage units since 2008." articles.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's ‘Ramayana’ has not only made its mark at the international box office, but the film is already gaining recognition from award shows.
articles.body: Nitesh Tiwari's ‘Ramayana’ has not only made its mark at the international box office, but the film is already gaining recognition from award shows. According to the latest reports, the film has secured spots in two technical categories on the shortlist for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards.The Critics Choice Association (CCA) announced the shortlists on Monday, with ‘Ramayana’, titled ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ in international markets, making the cut in the Best Visual Effects and Best Stunt Design categories. In the Best Visual Effects category, the Indian epic will compete with ‘Dune: Part Three’, ‘The Odyssey’, ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’, ‘Project Hail Mary’, ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ and ‘Wildwood’. Dan Glass has been credited for the film's visual effects.The film has also secured a place on the Best Stunt Design shortlist, alongside titles such as ‘Dune: Part Three’, ‘The Odyssey’, ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ and ‘Jackass: Best and Last’. The recognition marks a significant achievement for the Indian production, placing it among some of the year's most ambitious international cinematic projects.Christopher Nolan's ‘The Odyssey’ has emerged as one of the leading contenders, earning mentions in 11 of the 12 categories announced. Denis Villeneuve's ‘Dune: Part Three’ and the Spanish-language film ‘La Bola Negra’ have secured eight mentions each. Meanwhile, ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ and Laika's animated feature ‘Wildwood’ have made it to seven categories.While 'Ramayana' has been shortlisted, the film has not yet secured a nomination in the two categories. It is now among the 59 films across 144 places in 12 categories selected by a special nominating committee. articles.title: Artesã que fez look de crochê de Anitta também já vestiu Xuxa | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao g1, Milena Guerke, crocheteira em Rancharia, no interior de SP, relembra como o convite para desenvolver as blusas para a ‘rainha dos baixinhos’ e vovó do ano aconteceu.
articles.summary: Mãe e artesã, Milena Guerke, de Rancharia (SP), voltou à infância ao ser convidada para confeccionar duas peças de crochê para a Xuxa.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Mãe e artesã, Milena Guerke voltou à infância ao ser convidada para confeccionar duas peças de crochê para Xuxa . Com ateliê em Rancharia (SP), a crocheteira também já teceu o look usado por Anitta no Grammy Latino deste ano .

Ao g1 , Milena relembra como o convite para desenvolver as blusas para a “rainha dos baixinhos” e vovó do ano aconteceu. Ela afirma que o contato começou a partir da assessoria de Bia Zany, que a apresentou a Marcelo Cavalcante, estilista da Xuxa.

“Quando ele entrou em contato comigo, confesso que fiquei sem acreditar! A princípio, o convite era para produzir uma gola colorida e que seria usada para o comercial do álbum XSPB14 Cores.”

Artesã de Rancharia (SP), Milena Guerke faz look de crochê utilizado por Xuxa — Foto: Milena Guerke/Arquivo pessoal/Reprodução internet

A conversa entre a artesã do interior de São Paulo e o estilista da artista ocorreu no início de 2025, antes do lançamento do “Xuxa Só para Baixinhos 14: Cores”.

“Conforme fomos conversando e ele foi conhecendo melhor meu trabalho, surgiu a ideia de fazer algo maior. Foi então que Marcelo decidiu que, em vez da gola, produziríamos uma blusa. A gola, portanto, não chegou a ser feita”, conta.

Segundo Milena, Marcelo lhe enviou um croqui com a proposta de modelagem e lhe deu liberdade para explorar o crochê, sugerindo pontos, tramas e texturas que ela acreditava que valorizariam a peça.

“Produzi a primeira blusa em apenas sete dias e, depois que a enviei, Marcelo me contou que a Xuxa havia adorado! E o mais surpreendente foi que ela gostou tanto que Marcelo me procurou novamente, dessa vez com a proposta de uma blusa arco-íris. Em mais uma semana, a segunda peça também estava pronta”, relembra.

As peças foram produzidas por Milena e enviadas em março de 2025, em duas etapas, conforme cada uma ficou pronta. “Eu fui uma baixinha da Xuxa! Cresci acompanhando seus programas, sempre fui fã e jamais imaginei que um dia teria a oportunidade de produzir roupas para ela.”

“Fiz cada ponto com muito amor, carinho e dedicação. Não era simplesmente mais um trabalho. Existia ali um sentimento muito especial, uma mistura de realização profissional com um sonho de infância. E quando veio o convite para produzir a segunda blusa, minha alegria foi ainda maior.”

Artesã de Rancharia (SP), Milena Guerke faz look de crochê utilizado por Xuxa — Foto: Milena Guerke/Reprodução

Xuxa enviou um vídeo elogiando e agradecendo às produções feitas por Milena. O conteúdo foi publicado no Instagram da artesã. Assista no início da reportagem.

“As cores sempre estiveram muito presentes no universo da Xuxa e hoje são também a essência da minha identidade artística. Mas, para mim, elas carregam um significado que vai muito além do crochê.”

Mãe de dois meninos de 10 anos, Milena conta que viver essa experiência ao lado deles tornou tudo ainda mais especial. Isso porque Vitório é autista e tem hiperfoco em cores.

“Enquanto eu tecia, ele ficava encantado, acompanhando os fios, as combinações e cada nova cor que surgia na peça. Era mágico para ele, e ver aquele encantamento me emocionava muito”, afirma.

Já Alexandre viveu tudo de outra maneira. “Ele ficou tão impressionado quando soube que eu estava fazendo uma roupa para a Xuxa que parecia não acreditar que aquilo estava realmente acontecendo.”

“Ver a surpresa e o entusiasmo dele me fez perceber que aquela conquista não era apenas minha. Meus filhos também estavam participando daquele sonho.”

Artesã de Rancharia (SP), Milena Guerke faz look de crochê utilizado por Anitta — Foto: Milena Guerke/Reprodução

Tecer os fios na prática também foi uma forma de tecer a arte na memória para Milena, ao relembrar a própria infância e o momento com os filhos. “Naquele momento, percebi que não estava apenas realizando um sonho da menina que fui.”

“Estava também construindo uma lembrança muito especial para os meus dois filhos. Costumo dizer que o crochê é minha terapia das cores. É através delas que encontro liberdade para criar, expressar sentimentos e transformar fios em arte.”

A partir das peças feitas, Milena conta que seu trabalho proporcionou a amizade com Marcelo Cavalcante, que é estilista da Xuxa. “O nosso querido Txielo, o que começou como uma parceria profissional se transformou em uma amizade muito especial, que levo com enorme carinho.”

“A Xuxa me proporcionou a realização de um sonho de infância, e esse trabalho também me presenteou com uma amizade que considero uma das grandes riquezas da minha caminhada na moda.”

Além desse trabalho, Milena já realizou outros feitos, como o figurino inspirado em Iemanjá, peças de Nossa Senhora e Cleópatra, apresentadas no Artesanal Fashion Day, bem como confeccionou looks para Gaby Spanic, atriz conhecida pela novela mexicana “A Usurpadora” , e para a cantora Fernanda Abreu.

Artesã de Rancharia (SP), Milena Guerke faz look de crochê utilizado por Anitta — Foto: Milena Guerke/Arquivo pessoal

No caso de Anitta , Milena confeccionou dois looks para a cantora. O figurino mais recente foi o utilizado pela artista brasileira no Grammy Latino, após vencer na categoria Melhor Álbum de Pop Contemporâneo em Língua Portuguesa.

Outro vestido feito por Milena já havia sido usado por Anitta em um dos clipes do álbum vencedor: “Ternura”, que exalta a conexão com Oxum, orixá protetora das águas doces, dos rios e das cachoeiras. A peça foi produzida em parceria com a marca Santa Resistência.

“Olhando para tudo isso, percebo que a arte me presenteou com muito mais do que oportunidades profissionais. Ela me trouxe pessoas, amizades, aprendizados e experiências que levarei para a vida inteira. Porque, no fim, o crochê não entrelaça apenas fios. Ele também entrelaça histórias, sonhos e pessoas”, completa Milena Guerke.

articles.title: Como é o show atual do Gorillaz, headliner do Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo traz turnê do álbum 'The Mountain', influenciado por música indiana. g1 assistiu ao show atual da banda e descreve como é a apresentação.
articles.summary: Grupo traz turnê do álbum 'The Mountain', influenciado por música indiana. g1 assistiu ao show atual da banda e descreve como é a apresentação.
articles.body:
Gorillaz vem ao Primavera Sound São Paulo com show do 'The Mountain', álbum influenciado por cultura indiana — Foto: Divulgação

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O Gorillaz é o headliner do Primavera Sound São Paulo 2026 e encerra a programação do festival no domingo (6).

O grupo é o único que passou ou vai passar por todas as franquias do festival espanhol neste ano: se apresentou em Barcelona, Porto, e segue para São Paulo e Buenos Aires.

O g1 assistiu ao show do grupo no festival Primavera Sound Barcelona, no dia 6 de junho. Foi um dos melhores, se não o melhor da edição, e promete ser igualmente excelente ao desembarcar por aqui. Veja como é o show:

Quem nunca viu um show do Gorillaz pode ficar na dúvida de como é o formato — afinal, a banda é representada por personagens fictícios e ilustrados. Na prática, o "desenho animado" aparece mais nos telões, muito bem usados, que dão a impressão de que os personagens estão cantando as músicas.

Mas quem sobe no palco são músicos de verdade, incluindo o carismático Damon Albarn (conhecido também pelo grupo Blur), que está mais soltinho que nunca.

Em Barcelona, usando traje militar, ele se jogou na galera, reclamou dos celulares, brincou com a câmera e cantou boa parte do tempo usando uma espécie de walkie-talkie.

Desta vez, a banda vem com o repertório atualizado. O grupo lançou "The Mountain", álbum influenciado por música indiana e com pegada espiritual, em março. Com isso, o show incorpora uma robusta banda com cítaras, flautas e um corpo de cantores.

Em Barcelona, ainda trouxeram vários convidados, incluindo Little Simz, que tinha se apresentado mais cedo no festival, a sul-africana Moonchild Sanelly e o rapper Yasiin Bey (anteriormente conhecido como Mos Def). Fica a curiosidade para saber quem eles convidariam (ou trariam?) por aqui.

Damon Albarn, do Gorillaz, se apresenta no Mita Festival em São Paulo — Foto: Alex Woloch/Divulgação

Em comparação com a última vinda do Gorillaz ao Brasil (o grupo veio em 2022 para o MITA Festival), o show está mais grandioso, estruturado e... meditativo, psicodélico, para combinar com a fase atual.

O grupo mescla bem as novas e antigas faixas, trazendo um tom oriental — quase de mantra — para tornar o repertório mais coeso. Sucessos como "Feel Good Inc" ganharam um novo arranjo, com o acréscimo de flautas no início.

E no caso das novas, até para quem não amou "The Mountain", o negócio funciona muito bem ao vivo, já que as músicas ficam ainda mais envolventes.

articles.title: Quem é Valéria Barcellos: atriz desabafou após vender só 21 ingressos | G1
articles.standfirst: Valéria Barcellos, conhecida por participar de novela da TV Globo, usou as redes sociais para expor preocupação com custos de evento em dezembro.
articles.summary: Conhecida como Luana Shine em Terra e Paixão, a artista Valéria Barcellos expõe a luta para pagar músicos e equipe após baixa adesão em evento em Porto Alegre.
articles.body:
Valéria Barcellos — Foto: Globo/João Miguel Júnior e arquivo pessoal

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A atriz e cantora Valéria Barcellos , de 46 anos, usou as redes sociais para fazer um desabafo após ser avisada de que apenas 21 ingressos para seu show , que ocorrerá no dia 16 de dezembro em Porto Alegre , tinham sido vendidos.

Ao g1 , afirmou que se sentiu frustrada. "Tentar produzir um show, pensar num show que aconteça de maneira grandiosa e ele estar se dirigindo para uma coisa que não vai ser aquilo que a gente esperava... Frustra, né?", diz.

Conhecida pela personagem Luana Shine na novela "Terra e Paixão", da TV Globo , Valéria é uma artista multifacetada. Um ano após a estreia na televisão, ela lançou o álbum "Saraval", em 2024 .

Sua carreira musical teve início ainda na infância. Ela relata que começou a se apresentar aos 6 anos. Entre os feitos que se destacam, estão a abertura do show da cantora Katy Perry na Arena do Grêmio, na capital gaúcha, em 2018; e uma apresentação em Paris , quando venceu o Festival da Canção Francesa, em 2012.

Natural de Santo Ângelo , a artista tem uma forte relação com Porto Alegre, onde se apresentava em bares e eventos. Valéria já ganhou o Troféu Mulher Cidadã da Assembleia Legislativa do Rio Grande do Sul , na categoria Mulher na Cultura, em 2016. Ela foi a primeira mulher trans a receber a premiação.

Atualmente, a gaúcha mora em São Paulo .

Valéria é lembrada também pela luta pelos direitos das pessoas LGBT+ . Em 2023, foi vítima de transfobia . Segundo relatado por ela na época, a segurança de um evento no Rio de Janeiro a impediu de entrar no banheiro feminino. Ela participava de uma festa de Halloween em um hotel e estava fantasiada de Freddie Mercury, vocalista da banda Queen .

Anos antes, em 2015, ela havia enfrentado outro episódio de violência. Foi atingida por chutes e ferida nas costas com uma chave de fenda quando passeava com o namorado na Cidade Baixa, em Porto Alegre.

Em 2020, Valéria descobriu que estava com câncer e passou por sessões de quimioterapia. Ela foi diagnosticada com um tumor chamado Sarcoma de Kaposi, um tipo raro que se forma nas paredes dos vasos sanguíneos e afeta a pele, mas também pode atingir os órgãos internos. A artista conseguiu se recuperar e retornar aos palcos.

Faltando pouco menos de um mês para o show em Porto Alegre (RS), a cantora fez publicações nas redes sociais para abordar a baixa adesão ao evento.

"Foi desesperador saber disso. Há toda uma infraestrutura a ser paga: músicos, técnicos, figurino, maquiagem... Tudo isso. É claro que eu e a produção sabíamos e sabemos dos riscos. Mas dói muito", escreveu no post, que soma mais de 1 milhão de visualizações e mais de 9 mil curtidas.

Cantora e atriz relata frustração após vender só 21 ingressos para show em Porto Alegre: 'Frustra, né?' — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A artista conta que a postagem teve o intuito de divulgar o evento e aumentar as vendas , mas não imaginava a repercussão. "A gente precisa vender mais. Acho que é isso que eu quis passar para as pessoas."

Ela destaca que sua maior preocupação era com as pessoas contratadas . "Como a gente ia ter que pagar essas pessoas e de onde eu ia tirar o dinheiro depois."

Apesar do número, ela não pretende cancelar o espetáculo .

"Eu ia fazer o show de qualquer maneira: para 20, para 10, para 5. Como já fiz para duas pessoas e para 30 mil no show da Katy Perry."

O show "ELA" reúne músicas e interpretações da atriz. Os ingressos têm valores que variam de R$ 95 a R$ 190. Até a manhã desta terça-feira (24), o número havia subido de 21 para 51 .

"O número de pessoas que tiver, vai ser lindo e vai brilhar da mesma maneira. O amor pela música vai ter que ser muito maior do que o número de pagantes, embora a gente precise dos pagantes. Mas esse show é uma celebração", conclui.

She admitted that his performance in 'Animal' had made her wonder whether she would be able to connect with him as Lord Ram. However, she said the actor had successfully overcome that concern."Watching #Ramayana late but finally! Here's my take! I just have to say the media is soooo misleading. articles.title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ star Tovah Feldshuh has ‘no animosity’ toward co-star despite Israel disagreement
articles.summary: Tovah Feldshuh says Adam Brody asked to meet her privately after his Israel "genocide" remarks, but the "Nobody Wants This" co-stars share no animosity.
articles.body: "Nobody Wants This" star Tovah Feldshuh said in a new interview that co-star Adam Brody asked for a private meeting with her following criticism of his remarks accusing Israel of "genocide." Speaking with Us Weekly ahead of a Paley Museum panel on Monday, Feldshuh said there is "no animosity" between her and Brody. She noted that she still considers him an "incredible friend," but that they remain in "profound disagreement" over the Middle East conflict. "After he said his comments, he asked to see me. So, we’ve talked privately about it," Feldshuh said, adding that she hopes Brody will eventually reconsider his view "based on fact and history." 'NOBODY WANTS THIS' STAR ACCUSES ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' The disagreement began in September when Brody, who identifies as Jewish and plays a rabbi on the Netflix series, told GQ Magazine that he believes Israel is committing a "genocide" in Gaza. He added, "put me down as wanting a free Palestine." Feldshuh, who plays Brody’s mother on "Nobody Wants This," pushed back against her co-star at the time, telling the New York Post that "to accuse the Jewish people of genocide is wild." She added that doing so is "right out of Hitler’s playbook. You take the victim, and you make the victim the perpetrator." RABBI WHO WORKED ON ADAM BRODY'S NETFLIX SHOW SLAMS ACTOR OVER GAZA COMMENTS Feldshuh told Us Weekly that she does not plan on publicly speaking out against Brody, saying that they are colleagues and can disagree with one another without "being disagreeable." "However, I’m sure everybody is very clear about how I stand and this isn’t a political statement. This is a statement based on whether or not I have a right to live," she added. ISRAELI ACTRESS CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD STARS 'SILENCING ARTISTS' WHO SUPPORT JEWISH STATE Feldshuh was not the only person behind the show to disagree with Brody. The series creator, Erin Foster, who converted to Judaism in 2019, previously said that she disagrees with Brody while praising the respectful dynamic among the cast. Speaking on the "Not Skinny But Not Fat" podcast in October, Foster said, "I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing." MICHAEL RAPAPORT TELLS CRAIG CARTON THAT HIS SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL HAS COST HIM WORK IN HOLLYWOOD She added, "While I love Adam, I also disagree with him. And that’s okay." Feldshuh acknowledged Foster's support in her new interview, telling Us Weekly she feels "lucky" the showrunner shares her perspective, and reiterated that she "will not cross swords with Adam." ROB LOWE CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD DOUBLE STANDARD AFTER FESTIVALS REJECT BEN SHAPIRO-WRITTEN FILM "He plays my son, and you know what else? He’s been an incredible friend to me. When they showed my documentary at the temple that hosted us, who came out of all the cast? Adam Brody. He sat next to me," she said. Entertainment critic Christian Toto praised Feldshuh’s approach, telling Fox News Digital that the actress prioritized the show and its crew over personal politics. "Kudos to Tovah for tackling this issue head on and not using the press to fight her battles. She's right, of course. We can all agree to disagree, and it shouldn't stop people from working together," Toto said. He added that while Feldshuh has "more wisdom and insight into the matter than Brody," keeping the peace on set shows that she "put her show and the many people who work on it above any personal vendettas." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Plus, ‘Nobody Wants This’ is a culture war weapon, in a way. The rom-com shows the Jewish community in a way that's flawed, funny and oh, so human. That's more important than her storming off the set or raging against her co-star," Toto said.

articles.title: Miss Universe 2026 Becomes First Mother to Win Pageant
articles.summary: Jennifer Barreto is also the sixth Miss Puerto Rico to win the title
articles.body:
Jennifer Barreto was crowned Miss Universe 2026 at the finals held in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and is the first mother to win the pageant

Fátima Bosch crowned her successor after representing the title for the last year

The pageant faced several controversies leading up to the finals, including visa issues for African contestants and injuries during rehearsals and events

Miss Universe has crowned its latest queen. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, the international pageant hosted its finals at Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and crowned Jennifer Barreto, who was competing to represent this year's host country, Puerto Rico. Barreto, 27, is a psychologist and social worker. She also has a daughter, Penelope, El Nuevo reported, and is the first mother to win the pageant. Miss Universe 2025 Fátima Bosch crowned her successor, bestowing the organization's newest crown, designed in collaboration between designer George Wittels and Maison d'OR, called "The Radiance of an Eternal Legacy," which features 3,150 diamonds set in 18-karat white gold.

Barreto was joined in the top five by Miss Universe Philippines, Miss Universe New Zealand, Miss Universe Venezuela and Miss Universe Dominican Republic.

Competitors came from more than 110 other countries and territories, including a few that had never participated in the final before, such as Miss Universe Saint Martin and Miss Universe Uganda. TV show host Mario Lopez and Miss Universe 2022 R'Bonney Gabriel hosted the fête. According to the hosts, this year's cast of 117 delegates was made up of 22 contestants with master's degrees, five doctors and 10 mothers. Contestants participated in multiple different activities in the lead-up to the pageant, including the customary closed-door interviews and the National Costume Competition and Preliminary Competition. During the night, the location for the 76th Miss Universe competition was also announced. Next year's competition will take place in Puerto Rico.

The lead-up to this year's Miss Universe pageant was buzzy, with news that some African contestants would not be able to participate due to visa restrictions and videos that surfaced of contestants stumbling down a makeshift beach walkway and another of Miss Universe France 2026 being wheeled out of a hotel in a wheelchair after injuring herself during rehearsals.

Last year's Miss Universe pageant was wracked by scandal after scandal, including fiery confrontations between Miss Universe executives and contestants, last-minute judge resignations, and even injuries.

Bosch's crowning came after the Miss Universe Organization found itself embroiled in several controversies in the lead-up to the pageant, including a livestream that went viral of pageant executive Nawat Itsaragrisil scolding Bosch for allegedly refusing to participate in a photo shoot meant for contestants to share on social media. Additionally, during last year's pageant, Miss Universe Jamaica Gabrielle Henry fell from the stage during the preliminary competition and could not compete in the rest of the competition. Later, it was revealed that Henry had sustained a traumatic brain injury. Later, Henry filed a lawsuit against the Miss Universe organization.

articles.title: John Travolta celebrates son Ben’s 16th birthday: ‘You are the sunshine of my life!!’
articles.summary: John Travolta shares a touching tribute on social media for his son Ben's 16th birthday, reflecting on family, love, and cherished memories.
articles.body: John Travolta just celebrated his son Ben’s 16th birthday. Taking to social media, the ‘Grease’ actor posted about the occasion, wished him a happy birthday, and shared an adorable picture of the two of them. Travolta shares Ben with his late wife, Kelly Preston, who passed away in 2020 after her battle with breast cancer.John Travolta wishes his son Ben on his 16th birthdayThe 71-year-old shared a photo of him smiling with his son on his Instagram account to celebrate his birthday. “Ben! You are the sunshine of my life!! Happy birthday, my son!! I love you,” Travolta wrote in his caption. His sister, Ella, also replied to the post and shared a few heart emojis. ‘Sleepless in Seattle’ star Rita Wilson also wrote “Happy Birthday, sweet Ben!” under the post to share her well wishes. Many fans and netizens also extended their wishes for the 16-year-old and flooded the comments section.Ben has two other siblings: Ella Bleu, who is 26 years old, and brother Jett, who passed away at age 16 in 2009 after suffering a seizure during a vacation trip to the Bahamas.John Travolta talks about being a fatherOver the years, Travolta has often talked about how proud and happy he is to be a father and has heavily praised his children on multiple occasions. Earlier this month, while in conversation with ExtraTV, the ‘Grease’ star talked about how Ben and Ella are the “ideal children."He also added, “My children are… It’s hard to find the words. But every parent dreams that they’d have these ideal children, and they live up to and beyond it. I can leave this lifetime knowing I’ve done well, and Kelly knowing that she did well. I really can say that. I’m very proud of them.”In 2021, he sat down for a conversation with Kevin Hart on his podcast ‘Hart to Heart,' sharing that people need to have some tough conversations with their children no matter what. He shared at the time that Ben had quite a lot of questions and fears about life after his brother Jett’s passing and his mother, Kelly’s passing. “He said, ‘Because Mom passed away, I’m afraid you’re going to,’ Travolta revealed. “And I said, ‘Well, it’s a very different thing,’ and I went through the differences of my longevity and her limited life,” Travolta recalled at the time.He continued talking about what he told Ben at the time and added, “‘But you know, Ben? You always love the truth, and I’m going to tell you the truth about life. Nobody knows when they’re going to go or when they’re going to stay.’ I said, ‘Your brother left at 16. Too young. Your mother left at 57; that was too young. But who’s to say?’ I said, ‘I could die tomorrow; you could—I mean, anybody can… It’s part of life… You don’t know exactly; you just do your best at trying to live the longest you can.'”Travolta and Preston met while doing a screen test for the 1987 film, ‘The Experts.’ They dated for a while and tied the knot in 1991. The two were together until the time of her passing six years ago. They welcomed their first son, Jett, in 1992, and their daughter, Ella, in 2000. articles.body: The debate surrounding the authenticity of Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' franchise has resurfaced after Retired Colonel Munishwar Nath Bakshi, popularly known as Hunny Bakshi, shared his views on the films.He clarified in a recent interview that although the story draws inspiration from actual incidents, its presentation has been shaped through creative imagination. The franchise has attracted considerable attention for its portrayal of geopolitical developments, national security issues and events connected to Pakistan. While some viewers have questioned the accuracy of its narrative, others have defended its depiction of real-world incidents.Speaking at the ANI National Security Summit, Colonel Hunny Bakshi (Retd) explained the distinction between actual events and their cinematic treatment. His comments come alongside earlier remarks by Pakistani journalist Arif Ajakia, who claimed that several incidents shown in the film reflected what he had witnessed in Lyari, Karachi.Retired Colonel Hunny Bakshi says 'Dhurandhar' is fiction based on real eventsRetired Colonel Munishwar Nath Bakshi said the franchise uses real incidents as its foundation but presents them through an imagined narrative. He explained that filmmakers often take inspiration from actual developments while creating a cinematic storyline around them."This is how we write now that I am a film guy; it is a fictitious story based on true events. Yes, the events happened; the narration is an imagination, but the events happened," he said.Hunny Bakshi jokes about his reaction to watching the filmColonel Hunny Bakshi (Retd) was also asked about his personal reaction to seeing incidents from real life recreated on the big screen. He responded with humour, suggesting that he might have celebrated with a drink had he not given up alcohol."Unfortunately tab tak maine daaru peeni chhod di thi. Nahi toh I would have gone home and had a drink."Aditya Dhar's 'Dhurandhar' franchise and its real-world referencesDirected by Aditya Dhar, the 'Dhurandhar' franchise stars Ranveer Singh and draws inspiration from geopolitical developments and national security-related events. The review acknowledged the film's scale and engaging storytelling while pointing out that its length and excessive presentation affected the overall experience.The review read, "Dhurandhar 2 cranks up the volume, violence, and ambition. It’s a well-crafted, engaging saga that, unfortunately, doesn’t know when to stop. Gripping yet overstuffed, it’s a relentless action extravaganza teetering on excess, best enjoyed as unrestrained work of fiction."Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'This is the fourth time I’ve experienced something unsettling ': Anupam Kher questions Mumbai air traffic congestion after flight diverts to Surat
articles.summary: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has raised concerns about air traffic congestion around Mumbai after his flight from Goa was diverted to Surat.
articles.body: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has raised concerns about air traffic congestion around Mumbai after his flight from Goa was diverted to Surat. The Air India aircraft had to abandon its landing attempt in Mumbai on Monday. Recalling the incident, Anupam Kher questioned whether better coordination between the city's two airports could prevent similar disruptions.The actor shared a video on X on Tuesday, explaining how the flight approached Mumbai but could not land as expected. He also said this was the fourth time in two years that he had experienced an unsettling situation while landing in the city. Kher clarified that he was not blaming the airline or its pilots, but wanted authorities to examine the challenges affecting Mumbai-bound flights.Anupam Kher recounts flight diversion from Mumbai to SuratAnupam Kher was travelling from Goa to Mumbai aboard Air India flight AI-2842 on Monday. According to his account, the aircraft was only around two minutes away from landing when it suddenly aborted its approach. The plane climbed again and circled in the air before the pilot informed passengers about the diversion.The announcement reportedly came after the aircraft could not continue holding because of limited fuel. Passengers were told that the flight would be redirected to Surat instead of attempting another landing in Mumbai.The aircraft reached Surat Airport at approximately 3:31 PM on November 23. It was refuelled and underwent the necessary checks before continuing its journey to Mumbai.Actor questions repeated landing disruptionsIn his post on X, Anupam Kher described the experience and explained why it had become a concern for him. He wrote, "I’m used to flight delays! Both in India and abroad! And most passengers learn to take them in their stride. But this is the fourth time I’ve experienced something unsettling while landing in Mumbai: just as the aircraft seems about to touch down, it takes off again, circles, and tries once more.This time, we couldn’t land in Mumbai and had to divert to Surat. I don’t blame the pilots or the airline; I’m sure they were doing what they had to do for everyone’s safety. But it does make me wonder: with two airports serving Mumbai, can we find a better way to manage the congestion on the ground and avoid this kind of chaos?A small complaint, perhaps! But mostly an observation from a passenger who would really like to land in Mumbai when the plane is ready to land. 😍🙏 @AAI_Official."Anupam Kher says repeated experiences have made him nervousAnupam Kher's latest experience has added to his concerns about flying into Mumbai. He said that similar incidents during the past two years had made him increasingly nervous about landing in the city.Mumbai's aviation network includes Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) and Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA). The latter has been developed to complement the existing airport and support the region's growing aviation requirements.Anupam Kher's remarks have brought the focus back to how effectively the two facilities can work together. Better coordination could help manage flight movements, ease pressure on existing infrastructure and improve the experience for passengers travelling to Mumbai.On the professional front, Anupam Kher is associated with Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Part 1', which released on November 5, 2026. The actor voices Jatayu, the giant bird from the epic, and also serves as the film's opening narrator.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Aamir Khan has reportedly begun an extensive preparation programme for his upcoming film 'Lalkaara', directed by Ashutosh Gowariker. The actor will portray legendary Indian cricketer Lala Amarnath in the sports drama. Set against the backdrop of the 1952 India-Pakistan Test series, the film will revisit an important chapter in the history of Indian cricket. Aamir Khan is currently undergoing cricket training with co-stars Vikrant Massey, Jitendra Kumar and Dhairya Karwa.The actors are reportedly practising at a heritage cricket club in South Mumbai. Two former Indian cricketers are training the cast for their respective roles. The coaches were also associated with the preparation of the actors in Kabir Khan's '83' (2021), which followed India's historic 1983 World Cup victory.January 4 shoot date has a 'Lagaan' connectionThe cricket sessions are expected to continue through November and December. The makers are planning to commence filming on January 4, 2027. The date holds particular significance for Aamir Khan and Ashutosh Gowariker. They began shooting their acclaimed film 'Lagaan' on January 4, 2000.The upcoming drama will focus on the 1952 Test series between India and Pakistan. It was the first cricket series between the neighbouring countries after the 1947 Partition. Aamir Khan will play Lala Amarnath, while Vikrant Massey is portraying Pakistani cricketer Abdul Hafeez Kardar.Reading sessions form part of the preparationThe cast's groundwork extends beyond physical training. The actors reportedly started reading sessions around mid-October to familiarise themselves with the characters and the film's historical setting.Aamir Khan has also held several discussions with writers Piyush Mishra and Neeraj Singh. The duo has written the story, screenplay and dialogues for the project. According to the report, the actor was impressed with the narrative during its initial narration.The report said, “Aamir has had several sittings with Piyush Mishra and Neeraj Singh, who have written the story, screenplay, and dialogues. 'Lalkaara' brings Aamir Khan and Ashutosh Gowariker together again after their association with 'Lagaan'.Aamir Khan shifts to Colaba for cricket practiceAamir Khan and his partner Gauri Spratt have reportedly moved into a luxury apartment in Colaba. The new address also offers easier access to a nearby cricket ground, allowing him to follow his training schedule without travelling long distances.According to Mid Day, “Aamir and Gauri Spratt have shifted to a luxury apartment in Colaba as the actor’s Bandra home is being renovated. articles.title: PETA protesters interrupt Rockettes' Christmas performance at Radio City Music Hall over use of live animals
articles.summary: PETA activists rushed the stage at Radio City Music Hall's "Christmas Spectacular," protesting the use of live camels, sheep and donkeys in the Nativity scenes.
articles.body: A trio of PETA activists crashed the Rockettes' performance at Radio City Music Hall in New York City on Tuesday in protest of the Christmas show's use of live animals in the Nativity scenes. The protesters disrupted Radio City Music Hall’s "Christmas Spectacular" because of the camels, sheep and donkeys used in the Nativity scenes. PETA said the animals were offstage during the demonstration against the "shameful" Nativity scenes that the group argues "exploited" the animals. During the demonstration, the activists rushed on stage with signs reading "Radio City: End Animal Acts Now!" and chanting the same message. "No more animals on stage!" one protester shouted as she ran up on stage in front of the performers, according to footage shared by PETA. ANIMAL RIGHTS ACTIVIST ATTACKS NYC HORSE CARRIAGE DRIVER WITH SKATEBOARD DURING TIRADE, UNION SAYS "Keep the camels and donkeys out of the performance!" another screamed. "Take the cruelty out of Christmas!" a third yelled. The three demonstrators were swiftly removed from the stage and hauled out by security. PETA said it took issue with the show subjecting the live animals to flashing lights and loud noises, including fireworks and cheering crowds. "Unlike the Rockettes, the camels, sheep, and donkeys exploited for the Christmas Spectacular didn’t sign up for bright lights, roaring crowds, and the chaos of the stage, which can be confusing and downright terrifying for them," PETA President Tracy Reiman said in a statement. "PETA is calling on Radio City Music Hall to listen to the growing chorus demanding that it stop exploiting animals as living set pieces and let talented human performers or clever stagecraft steal the show," Reiman continued. The animal rights group also claimed that the animals used in the performance undergo stressful transport and are confined backstage, including some reportedly kept in the basement, when they are not performing during the show’s months-long run every winter. In a statement to Fox News Digital, Radio City Music Hall said PETA "deliberately attempted to disrupt today’s performance, endangering our performers and interfering with the experience of our guests." "We have zero tolerance for this behavior and will pursue all available legal action against anyone who engages in such conduct," the statement continued. HUNDREDS OF ACTIVISTS FACE PEPPER SPRAY IN VIOLENT CLASH WITH DEPUTIES AT WISCONSIN BEAGLE RESEARCH FACILITY The disruption during Tuesday's show was PETA's latest attempt to pressure Radio City into ending the use of live animals for shows. Nearly 40,000 PETA supporters have called on Chase, Lexus, SpotHero and Verizon to end their sponsorships for the show until it stops using live animals. articles.title: 'Gunmaaster G9' director Aditya Datt admits Emraan Hashmi’s 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne' comes with 'huge baggage'
articles.summary: ‘Gunmaaster G9’ marks the reunion of Emraan Hashmi and Aditya Datt, 20 years after their last film together, ‘Dil Diya Hai’.
articles.body: ‘Gunmaaster G9’ marks the reunion of Emraan Hashmi and Aditya Datt, 20 years after their last film together, ‘Dil Diya Hai’. In the actioner, Emraan plays a secret operative caught in a dangerous underworld of firearms, espionage and personal conflict. Aditya has now opened up about working with one of his best friends again after all this time, and why the two stayed away from each other professionally for so long.Aditya Datt on Emraan Hashmi projects that fell apartIn a chat with News18, Aditya shared that ‘Gunmaaster G9’ could have been his sixth film with Emraan had their last three projects come together. "After 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne' and 'Dil Diya Hai', we tried coming together a few times. For one reason or the other, things fell apart at the last minute. In fact, we tried locking three scripts. We were about to take them on floors but none of them worked out," he said.Aditya continued, "I then got busy with Commando 3 and Table No 21. Emraan, anyway, is super busy. So, each time, we locked a script and were about to shoot, some mess would crop up. But like they say, there's a time for everything. So, we waited for the right time." One thing he was "clear" about, though, was that his next outing with Emraan would be a full-on masala action film, a shift from the two romantic thrillers they had done before.“When Emraan and I were thinking about what to do, I told him I can’t do normal anymore. I like portraying my leads as stars. I don’t want to do slice-of-life. If you look at Emraan’s career graph in the last couple of years, he was trying to do realistic cinema. I wanted to present him as a larger-than-life action hero. Interestingly, we connected on this genre and this time around, things fell into place," Aditya stated.Himesh Reshammiya returns for 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne' trio‘Gunmaaster G9’ also brings together Emraan, Aditya and Himesh Reshammiya again after 20 years. Aditya reveals that having Himesh on board wasn't the initial plan. "When I finished the script, I had shortlisted a couple of songs by other music directors," he recalls, putting the reunion down to a chance encounter with the musician and a bit of destiny. On whether he felt the weight of matching the Aashiq Banaya Aapne craze, he said, "Yes, it comes with huge baggage. I told Emraan and Himesh that let's just have fun without getting trapped into that pressure of expectations. The only thing we stuck to was bringing that freshness and spark that we had during Aashiq Banaya Aapne. We sat on each song for 2-3 months," he shares.“The music of Aashiq Banaya Aapne created history and we knew there would be comparison. We wanted to give audiences the same feeling without copying the music of Aashiq Banaya Aapne. The easiest thing would be to pick up songs from that film, rehash and release them. That temptation could’ve been there. But then I said that we aren’t going to take that route," Aditya said.'Gunmaaster G9' release date and cast‘Gunmaaster G9’ features Genelia Deshmukh and Aparshakti Khurana in key roles. articles.title: Miguel Ángel Revilla renuncia a ‘La cena de los idiotas’ con Gonzalo Miró: “Le metió la pistola en la cabeza
articles.standfirst: José Manuel Margallo, Baltasar Garzón y Cristina Almeida sí participan
articles.summary: José Manuel Margallo, Baltasar Garzón y Cristina Almeida sí participan
articles.body: El pasado martes, 24 de noviembre, el programa ‘La cena de los idiotas’ de RTVE emitió una nueva entrega y, en esta ocasión, la velada se tuvo que dividir en dos porque Miguel Ángel Revilla, uno de los invitados de Gonzalo Miró, no quiso continuar y unirse al resto de participantes: José Manuel Margallo, Baltasar Garzón y Cristina Almeida. La noche comenzó con el expresidente de Cantabria queriendo hablar sobre las diferencias entre la vida de antes y la de ahora. Fue entonces cuando reveló su infancia no fue sencilla, no comiendo su primer plátano hasta los 10 años y sufriendo por los golpes de los curas con la madera. “A mi hermano casi le sacan un ojo. Cogió mi padre una pistola que tenía en casa, nos llevó a los hermanos a ver al cura, le metió la pistola en la cabeza y le advirtió que no volviera a hacer eso”, contaba Revilla, que pasó a negarse a quedarse a la cena y obligó a Gonzalo Miró a buscar una salida. Con la llegada del resto de invitados, el presentador pudo sentarse a la mesa y hacer una cena en condiciones. Margallo quiso destacar algo sobre lo que espera a las nuevas generaciones: “Los jóvenes van a vivir peor que los padres”. “Va como un tiro la economía hacia fuera, pero la de dentro, no”, aseveró Almeida. “Yo me tiraba contando chistes seis horas seguidas, pero esta faceta se me fue después de pasar por la política”, reveló Garzón, que explicó que su mayor error de juventud fue comprar discos de la resistencia durante un viaje a Roma, lo que provocó un castigo considerable. Almeida, por su parte, dijo que casarse por segunda vez no había salido bien y Margallo habló sobre la compra de un traje para disfrazarse en las fiestas de moros y cristianos: “Las redes sociales me machacaron”, reconoció.

articles.title: McLaren vende a un megamillonario su Fórmula 1 de 2027 antes de que lo conduzcan Norris o Piastri
articles.standfirst: El próximo 9 de diciembre va a subastar una unidad que correrá en la próxima temporada de Fórmula 1, pero hay una cláusula muy importante que el comprador tendrá que aceptar
articles.summary: El próximo 9 de diciembre va a subastar una unidad que correrá en la próxima temporada de Fórmula 1, pero hay una cláusula muy importante que el comprador tendrá que aceptar
articles.body: "El coche con el que ese piloto acaba de ganar la carrera es mío". Suena a fanfarronada, pero es lo que podrá decir con toda la razón del mundo un multimillonario en 2027 después de, por ejemplo, ver la carrera desde su yate amarrado en el puerto de Mónaco o en el de Yas Marina. Si estamos acostumbrados a que, de cuando en cuando, algunas escuderías vendan sus coches de Fórmula 1 para aligerar su garaje y hacer caja, lo que va a hacer McLaren en esta ocasión es diferente: el próximo 9 de diciembre va a sacar a subasta no un coche con un historial en competición, sino uno que tiene toda su historia por hacer. Aunque tampoco es algo nuevo en este equipo, porque en 2025 ya vendió de antemano una unidad del coche de 2026. El coche que va a sacar a subasta es un McLaren MCL41 con el que el equipo de Woking va a participar en la próxima temporada de Fórmula 1. No una unidad extra que el equipo vaya a hacer para que el comprador se lo lleve inmaculado a su casa, sino uno de los que van a ser empleados a lo largo del año por Norris o Piastri. La venta se va a realizar por subasta de RM Sotheby's y se va a llevar a cabo desde Abu Dabi, aunque esta vez no habrá coche expuesto por la sencilla razón de que todavía no está construido y aún habrá que esperar hasta el nuevo año para que sea presentado. Los coleccionistas con mayor músculo económico podrán pujar por teléfono, y el ganador tendrá que elegir, antes de que el coche sea construido, si quiere una unidad conducida por Norris o por Piastri... Teniendo en cuenta que uno ha sido campeón del mundo y el otro no, la elección parece fácil. El coche vendrá completo, con los colores de la temporada 2027 y el motor Mercedes AMG, cuya potencia se desconoce. Pero ningún equipo quiere que otras escuderías copien su última tecnología, así que McLaren ha dejado claro que su propietario no lo podrá recibir hasta el final de la temporada 2029. Lo que sí hará el equipo de Woking mientras tanto es entregar una unidad 'de exposición', un coche sin motor y sin las últimas mejoras técnicas en aerodinámica, pero sí similar en líneas generales al del coche con el que correrá el año próximo, para que al propietario se le haga más llevadera la espera. Además, el comprador podrá conocer a Zak Brown, Lando Norris y Oscar Piastri y será invitado a visitar Woking antes de la temporada 2027, a la puesta de largo del nuevo coche, a dos Grandes Premios (uno de ellos, Mónaco), a las 24 Horas de Le Mans y a las 500 Millas de Indianápolis. Y muy interesante es el hecho de que el ganador de la puja, una vez que reciba su coche, no tendrá que conformarse con tener el Fórmula 1 en un garaje o en un salón, sino que podrá utilizarlo en circuito cuantas veces quiera, ya que tendrá a su servicio (previo pago) a un equipo de ingenieros y mecánicos de McLaren a su disposición. Es difícil saber con exactitud por cuánto se va a vender el coche, pero los expertos de RM Sotheby's calculan que su precio final estará entre 8,2 y 10 millones de euros. Pero nos sirve de precedente el precio del coche de 2026 subastado en 2025 (que se entregará a su dueño en 2028), por el que pagaron 10,5 millones de euros.

articles.title: Ferran Adrià, chef, y su respeto a esta popular cadena de hamburguesas: "Yo a cuatro euros no sabría hacerlo mejor..."
articles.standfirst: El experto gastronómico analiza los restaurantes de comida rápida
articles.summary: El experto gastronómico analiza los restaurantes de comida rápida
articles.body: El nombre de Ferran Adrià está históricamente vinculado, por méritos propios, a la cocina creativa del más alto nivel. De todos modos, el chef catalán no es ajeno a la realidad gastronómica de muchos ciudadanos y se ha resistido a criticar las populares cadenas de hamburguesas, como McDonald's. "No me gusta, pero le tengo mucho respeto", ha comentado en 'Fuera de carta'. Ferran Adrià ha argumentado su opinión desde un estricto análisis culinario: "Porque yo a cuatro euros no sabría hacerlo mejor. Con carne de guayo (una de las más caras y populares del mercado) es muy fácil hacer una hamburguesa... A veinte euros, claro". El precio de un menú en las cadenas de comida rápida está muy por debajo del umbral de precio que comenta el experto ya que, entre otras cuestiones, apuestan por ingredientes con un coste menor para su clientela. El chef ha roto una lanza a favor de este tipo de restaurantes. "Los listillos que critican que vayan a por cuatro euros. Claro, porque es muy fácil... En España, el 95 por ciento de la gente no llega a final de mes bien. No se puede ser populista", ha recordado durante la entrevista en el citado pódcast. "Dame 20 euros para poder hacer una hamburguesa y le hago de lo que usted quiera", ha insistido. Ferran Adrià ha comentado que él no es consumidor habitual de este tipo de productos, como los que ofrece la citada cadena de comida rápida en sus locales, pero ha apuntado que, como profesional de la gastronomía, está obligado a conocerlos: "Yo no lo como, pero lo tienes que probar. Y las patatas fritas, que ya sé que son congeladas, pero a veces son mucho mejor que en sitios que las hacen frescas". El chef catalán ha repetido que tiene un gran respeto por estos negocios.

articles.body: Netflix unveiled the trailer of its first-ever Pakistani original series, Momina Duraid’s 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo', at a grand event in Karachi on Tuesday. The launch witnessed the presence of several prominent names from the Pakistani entertainment industry, including Fawad Khan, Hania Aamir, Sanam Saeed, Ahad Raza Mir, Bilal Ashraf, Iqra Aziz, Maya Ali and Hamza Abbasi. However, Mahira Khan who is expecting her second baby was absent from the event.The launch also saw the cast speak about the significance of the project and what its global release. “I don’t think this journey would’ve been as beautiful with anyone else. As soon as the trailer was dropped, The All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has demanded a long-term legal ban on Pakistani films, television shows and artists appearing on Indian screens. The demand comes ahead of the series' scheduled release on December 4, 2026. The association shared the letter on X, stating that it had raised the matter with the Centre and that national interests should take priority over entertainment. It also urged Netflix India not to stream Pakistani content on its platform.Amid this, while speaking to the media on the red carpet, Fawad expressed hope that the show's release would create further opportunities for actors and storytellers from Pakistan. He pointed out that Pakistani dramas already enjoy a substantial international following, with several shows finding audiences beyond the country's borders.“As it is, the audience of Pakistani dramas is very wide and spread across the globe. A lot of them get translated in other languages too. There are some shows which have worked on Netflix too, like Humsafar and Zindagi Gulzar Hai,” he said.The actor also highlighted how Netflix could help the series reach audiences in several countries while taking Pakistani stories to a wider platform.“People have been watching Pakistani shows all this while. Now, it’s just going to reach more people in 191 countries and in a larger-than-life picture. It’s not just one representation of Pakistan. articles.title: Hundreds complain about I'm A Celebrity after Mariella Frostrup called AJ Odudu 'aggressive'
articles.summary: More than 800 viewers complain to regulator Ofcom after a row between AJ Odudu and Mariella Frostrup.
articles.body:
More than 800 people have complained to the media regulator about an episode of ITV reality show I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! in which Mariella Frostrup accused her campmate AJ Odudu of being "aggressive".

Tensions first flared between the pair as they were seen cooking together on Saturday, before both were reduced to tears when the friction escalated the following morning.

Ofcom said 887 people had filed complaints about Sunday's episode in relation to "alleged bullying behaviour" by Frostrup towards Odudu.

The pair were seen clearing the air on Tuesday, with broadcaster Frostrup saying she was "sorry for calling you aggressive" and Odudu telling her it is "a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women".

An Ofcom spokesperson told BBC News: "We are assessing the complaints against our rules, but are yet to decide whether or not to investigate."

In Sunday's instalment of the programme, Odudu said she felt being called aggressive was "very harsh" and it was "an insane word" to use about her, and that "it is just such a triggering word".

In an amicable conversation in Tuesday's episode, she told Frostrup: "It's triggering because in this world, navigating it as a person who looks like me can be difficult sometimes because my experience is that my emotions and my intent are completely misconstrued.

"In same way that you are allowed to express yourself, I can't express myself in the same way. We're not granted the same freedom.

"You're allowed to be emotional and passionate, and I automatically go to 'aggressive'. There's no in-between. It's like I'm 'dramatic' and 'aggressive' and that's it.

"Whereas I feel like someone like you gets to go through all the emotions of life and all of those emotions are accepted and embraced and valid."

Frostrup replied that she thought being labelled "agressive" was "a woman thing more than anything else".

Odudu responded: "I do definitely see your point and agree with it, but those words stick as well. Those words can stick for us. The moment passes for you and it doesn't pass for me."

Signs of friction resurfaced when Frostrup told Odudu that "you don't take an apology well".

Odudu added: "It's good you asked, but it's a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women."

Many viewers defended Odudu after the pair's earlier encounter.
